findings.location: docs/feature/iis-slack-replace-remove/acceptance.md ### S3, the row bound to crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature :: Remove says how many workspaces stop posting, and reading it removes nothing (handoff.json acceptance.S3 row 2, obligations L6/F203)
findings.obligation: L6/F203: GET the remove door twice with a saved app leaves the row, the activity list and the configuration version unchanged (P4: the remove page changes nothing, including when prefetched)
findings.observation: Carried forward from the accepted review and now narrowed by what the candidate shipped: the version clause has a witness, but no row cites it. The only test F203 cites is the public scenario, whose closing step then_saved_app_unchanged reads the page, both secrets, the activity list, Add to Slack and a verifying event - never the configuration version. The witness is crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/instance.rs:1934 the_table_of_what_the_confirm_and_remove_pages_reach_when_they_are_only_read, which at HEAD asserts ReadOnlyDoor::SlackRemove.reads() == [PageRead::ConnectedWorkspaces] - a read-only set - and show_slack_remove (:1071) takes its one store access through that same ReadOnlyDoor::SlackRemove.read(&store), so a version-bumping read would have to name a write the table does not list. That test is still cited only for L6/F201 and L6/F202, by an S2 row whose stimulus text names the confirm page alone, so read from the record F203 version clause is unobserved while in the candidate it is observed. The completeness relation holds in fact and fails on paper.
findings.remediation: Cite L6/F203 at crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/instance.rs :: the table of what the confirm and remove pages reach when they are only read, either by adding an S3 row for that table over the remove door or by extending the S2 row obligations and its stimulus text to the two doors it now reads. No test needs writing; only the binding and the stimulus text are wrong.

findings.location: docs/feature/iis-slack-replace-remove/architecture.md #### D16 (handoff.json design.decisions D16, fact F657; governed slices S1, S2, S3)
findings.obligation: A user-visible claim a design decision makes needs an obligation or case an oracle can observe: D16 promises that an address alone - typed again, bookmarked or shared - carries neither a submitted value nor a notice, so the page claims no change that was not made
findings.observation: D16 was recorded at 371398e with no obligation, case or law citing it, and nothing in the candidate observes the half of it that is more than the redirect. Across the S3 rows no obligation names D16; no scenario opens the integrations page a second time after a change, nor reaches it by address alone, to read that the notice is gone; and no unit test covers SavedNotice::taken_from taking the value out (grep over handlers/instance.rs shows taken_from named only at :432 and :846, in production code). The scenarios observe that a change lands on the integrations page with its notice, which a handler that kept the notice in the address, or left it in the session for every later reading, would also pass. So the one false-claim outcome D16 exists to prevent - a shared or retyped address reading "Removed. Slack is not set up on this Foundry." when nothing was removed - has no falsifier. The S3 oracle bytes predate D16 and cite no such obligation, so this is not an oracle omission.
findings.remediation: Bind D16 to something observable or scope it out explicitly: state its consequence as a case of an existing law (the notice is read once and an address carries none) so the oracle can add the second reading to an existing scenario, or record in D16 that the one-shot property is unobservable at this slice and name where it is observed. Non-blocking for craft, which is complete; it stays a completion obligation until the claim is either observed or scoped.

observations.text: Re-review at 371398e, no new execution: the oracle and its three supports are byte-identical to the bytes accepted at 2f9d415. sha256 of instance-integration-setup.feature 6a33d474b2a11becf26a8530c62001941a5e222fe8e875b9cde7f3164d9c8004, steps/feature_instance_integration_setup.rs da2811eeb3fb133bea8b3215257bc68be812c723e8041120da45f7f369c00454, support/instance_integration_setup.rs 2fc4d9c8514d0bfb7046ca9f1c16eef120e20bd3c9cc1f7ad3616c37394398a1, support/external_integration_plugins.rs e25df60c7072cba8da4bc71f1d108df53c2bc9cd477d032fa932ccaab2f59dfa; git log --oneline 2f9d415..HEAD over those four paths is empty and git diff --stat 2f9d415..HEAD -- crates/foundry-acceptance is empty (both exit 0), so the whole acceptance crate is unchanged and no shared step was weakened or redefined. git status --porcelain reports only the untracked docs/feature/iis-slack-replace-remove/.nwdes-drafts/ directory, which I did not touch. The semantic RED recorded for this oracle at revision 2f9d415 (29 scenarios, 20 passed, 9 failed; 341 steps, 332 passed, 9 failed; 0 parsing and 0 hook errors) therefore remains the evidence for these same bytes; I executed no cargo, lane or test command in this review. The GREEN of the us-iis-05 lane at e941b18 (29/29) is the crafter and whole-candidate reviewer evidence that the root supplied, not an execution of mine.

The reviewed delta since the accepted S3 oracle review is exactly four changes, all in docs at 371398e (git show --stat 371398e, exit 0): (1) acceptance row 6 "Setting the same app up again finds Canzan Labs still connected" restated (stimulus F663, expected F664, user result F665, still_passes_if F666) and bound for the first time to an obligation, L3/F661; (2) acceptance row 7 "Once the Slack app is removed no replica accepts Slack events any more" stimulus replaced (F585 -> F667); (3) law L3 restated (F179 -> F660, three closed facts instead of two) with case F661 added and its reason restated (F185 -> F662); (4) decisions D16, D17, D18 recorded, D16 governing S1, S2 and S3. The production commits c271cf6 and e941b18 touched no oracle or support byte. I judged only this delta and the obligations it affects, retaining the prior judgments on the nine S3 scenarios, on step closure and on the pre-existing bindings.

Row 6 observes amended case L3/F661 and distinguishes it. F661 is "NewApp with 1 connected workspace left behind by a removed app, no app in effect: saved at once, no pending row, and no confirm page naming an empty client ID". The scenario at crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature:1011 constructs exactly that state - the saved app, "Priya has connected Canzan Labs to Slack with this Foundry app", then "Priya has removed the Slack app", so one connection is left behind and no app is in effect - and submits the same client ID with both secrets. Its two Thens falsify the held-for-confirm alternative twice: reading "Saved. Workspace admins can now choose Add to Slack." is unreachable from the I-14 confirm page a held submission answers, and the workspace page reading "Connected to Canzan Labs" needs an app in effect, which a hold would not have stored. The "no pending row" and "no confirm page naming an empty client ID" clauses are additionally read, at the handler, by the gate table crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/instance.rs:1784, which at HEAD asserts SubmissionDoor::of(NewApp, connected, AppInEffect::None) == SaveAtOnce for counts 0, 1, 2, 3 and 137, so the amended third fact of L3 is read over its whole count partition and not only at n = 1.

The second finding of the accepted S3 review is resolved by the delta. Row 7 stimulus now reads "This Foundry runs as two replicas on one database, each of them holding the Slack app the instance admin entered, and she removes it." and no longer claims a connected workspace. The scenario at instance-integration-setup.feature:1022 constructs precisely that: two replicas with the operator instance key, the secrets key generated, "every replica has the Slack app 6123456789012.7234567890123 in effect", then the removal, with no connect step. The law observation L9/F217 is unchanged and still read by then_no_replica_verifies, which asks each replica at its own address inside the 60 s bound. I close that finding.

Changed-by-design test files, judged by their bytes at HEAD: the unit and store tests the S3 rows cite all resolve, including the three that the prior review recorded as not yet existing. crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/instance.rs:1859 the_table_of_the_controls_the_page_offers_over_each_app_in_effect still reads all five app-in-effect cases, so L5/F196 (environment app, no saved row) and L5/F198 (no app in effect) keep their observations, and each case still asserts SlackOffer::Remove.applies(effect, mode) == offers_nonempty, the same predicate the door itself uses (removable() at :1130), so "the POST changes nothing" is not a separate claim. instance.rs:1784 the gate and count-form table, slack_app.rs:691 the_table_of_which_secrets_a_submission_keeps_and_which_it_replaces, slack_app.rs:565/615/626/635 the four field tests, iis_instance_store.rs:739 slack_save_fences_on_the_sealing_key and iis_instance_store.rs:990 the superseded-key table all exist. e941b18 dropped exactly one handler test, each_slack_offer_names_its_own_door, which asserted SlackOffer label/door/opens match arms; no acceptance row cites it, and the door it restated is observed publicly by the scenarios that follow the page Remove control to the remove page and post it. No weakening.

Jev: typesafe unavailable. I batched four reviewer-owned questions over compact redacted state (does row 6 distinguish F661 from the held-for-confirm alternative; is the amended replica stimulus truthful about the state its scenario builds; what is the state of F203 version clause; which owner should resolve the unbound D16 claim) and ran python3 /Users/jeffbailey/.claude/skills/nw-typesafe-system-one/scripts/jev_decide.py --request <scratchpad request> --output - : stdout "typesafe: unavailable (TYPESAFE_API_KEY is absent from this process environment...)", stderr empty, exit 3. No retry, no fabricated judgment; all four questions were decided locally against the original bytes and are recorded in these observations and findings. Test-time budget: no finding, the reviewed bytes are unchanged and add no statement or measurement of per-test time, so the nine-run median evidence is not called for.

D16 does not invalidate the S3 observations it governs. The removal now answers post, redirect, get with I-16 left as a one-shot value in the admin session (SavedNotice::answered / taken_from, crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/instance.rs:402-440, read back at :846; the former ?saved= query reader saved_notice() was deleted in e941b18). The unchanged scenario "Removing the Slack app says Slack is gone and records who removed it" asserts both halves of that answer - Priya reads "Removed. Slack is not set up on this Foundry." and Priya is on the instance integrations page - so it observes the notice through whichever carrier the design chose and reads the redirect landing, which the crafter us-iis-05 lane confirms green at e941b18. What D16 adds beyond that is the subject of my design finding.

diagnostic: Re-approved at 371398e. The S3 public oracle is unchanged: the feature file and all three supports are byte-identical to the bytes accepted at 2f9d415 and the whole acceptance crate shows an empty diff since then, so no scenario was rewritten, no shared step was weakened or redefined, and the semantic RED recorded at that revision still is the evidence for these bytes - reused with the byte comparison above, not restamped as a new run; I executed no lane. The delta is four doc changes, all sound. Row 6 is now bound to the amended L3 case F661 and really observes it: the scenario builds a connection left behind by a removed app with no app in effect, and its two readings - the saved notice, unreachable from the I-14 confirm page, and the workspace page still reading Connected to Canzan Labs, impossible without a stored app - falsify the held-for-confirm alternative twice, while the handler gate table reads SaveAtOnce for AppInEffect::None over the whole count partition. The row 7 stimulus correction closes the second finding of the prior review: it now describes exactly the two-replica state with no workspace connected that the scenario builds, and L9/F217 is still read at each replica address inside the 60 s bound. L3 restated to three closed facts loses no case: every conjunct of the gate is falsified once and the positive case is read over both apps in effect. D17 and D18 govern S1 and S2. D16 governs S3 and does not disturb what the oracle observes: the removal answer still reads I-16 and the integrations page landing, whichever carrier the notice takes. Two non-blocking findings stay open and neither loses a promised outcome at this phase. The oracle finding is the carried-forward L6/F203 one, now narrowed to a binding defect: the configuration-version clause is genuinely witnessed by the read-only-door table that the remove handler routes its only store access through, but no row cites that table for F203, so the completeness relation holds in fact and fails on paper. The design finding is new: D16 promises that an address alone claims no change that was not made, and that promise has no obligation, no case and no falsifier anywhere in the candidate. Both are completion obligations. Jev was unavailable (TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent, exit 3); the four questions I formed were decided locally against the original bytes. No implementation and no product finding.
